title: Say it once

creation.briefMd: A greeting that uses a name.

blocks.md:
## Print is a tool

Print is a tool for showing a message, not the message itself. The greeting lives in the values you already have — here a `name` — and `print` only sends that line to the screen. Build the line from the name so changing the name changes the greeting without rewriting the sentence by hand.

This bites when you type `Hello, Ada!` as a frozen string and ignore `name`. The first run looks right. Rename the person to `Grace` and the line still says Ada, because the program never read the variable. A greeting that cannot follow its own data is just a poster.

```python
name = "Ada"
print(f"Hello, {name}!")
```

A common mistake is printing a fixed `"Hello"` or a hardcoded full greeting. That treats print as the whole program. The exercise asks you to print `Hello, Ada!` by using the `name` value — an f-string is a good tool — so the output includes Ada because of the variable, not because you copied the letters.

hintLadder.md: The output must include the name Ada from the variable.
